test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 22 Oct, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: By selling an article for ₹19, a dealer makes a profit of 10%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 40%?
solution:
**Given:**

Selling price (SP) = ₹19

Profit percentage (P₁) = 10%

New profit percentage (P₂) = 40%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP × (100 / (100 + Profit%))

New Selling Price (SPₙₑw) = CP × (100 + New Profit%) / 100

Increase in Selling Price = SPₙₑw - SP

**Calculation:**

CP = SP × (100 / (100 + P₁))

⇒ CP = 19 × (100 / (100 + 10))

⇒ CP = 19 × (100 / 110)

⇒ CP = 19 × 0.9091 = ₹17.27

SPₙₑw = CP × (100 + P₂) / 100

⇒ SPₙₑw = 17.27 × (100 + 40) / 100

⇒ SPₙₑw = 17.27 × 140 / 100

⇒ SPₙₑw = 17.27 × 1.4 = ₹24.18

Increase = SPₙₑw - SP

⇒ Increase = 24.18 - 19 = ₹5.18

**The dealer should increase the selling price by ₹5.18.**
